title: Depth reduction for depth-one composed circuits
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ inputs of depth exactly $1$, and let $g_1,\dots,g_m \colon (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \bbf_2$ be Boolean functions on $n$ variables, each of which is computed by some DNF formula of width at most $l$ and also by some CNF formula of width at most $l$. Then the composed function $x \mapsto c\big(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\big)$ — obtained by feeding $g_i(x)$ into the $i$-th input of $c$ — is, up to an overall sign, computed by a single DNF formula of width at most $l$ each of whose terms has no repeated literal and mentions every variable at most once (in particular no term contains both a variable and its negation). Precisely, there exist such a DNF formula $\varphi$ and a sign bit $s$ so that, for every $x$, $\varphi(x) = c\big(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\big)$ when $s$ is positive and $\lnot\varphi(x) = c\big(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\big)$ when $s$ is negative.
hypotheses_covered: circuit c on m inputs has depth exactly 1
each of the m inputs is a Boolean function g_i on n variables
each g_i is computed by a DNF of width at most l
each g_i is computed by a CNF of width at most l
replaced:
A circuit $c$ of depth exactly $1$ over gates with width-$l$ DNF and CNF representations
collapses to a single signed gate: there exist a width-$l$ DNF $\varphi$ (with
duplicate-free, non-repeating-variable terms) and a sign bit whose signed evaluation
equals $c.\mathrm{eval}\,(\lambda i,\ \mathrm{gates}\,i\,x)$ for all $x$.
